$comment:
Numeric policy limits for the registry. Edit here, nowhere else — tools/ and bot/ both read this file. EVERY numeric cap in this file carries exactly one sibling saying what its relationship to an author's source tree is, and tools/validate.mjs refuses one that carries none — because the way three caps came to be enforced at ingest and mirrored nowhere was not a decision, it was an absence nobody could see. The four siblings:

`<name>_mirrors` — this number is a COPY of a constant in AstraPlugins/spec/limits.yaml, which the daemon also mirrors. It must equal it; validate.mjs compares them for real when an AstraPlugins checkout is reachable ($ASTRA_PLUGINS_DIR, else a sibling ../AstraPlugins) and prints a `note` saying the check did not run when neither exists, because a check that quietly did not happen must not look like a check that passed.

`<name>_mirrored_by` — an author CAN trip this cap from their own source tree, and a copy of the number lives in the file this names so `astra-plugin` can refuse it at pack time, BEFORE a tag exists. validate.mjs checks the copy is there and equal, and tools/check-locales.py --rules C20 checks it from the other end.

`<name>_not_author_facing` — nothing an author writes in a source tree decides this number, so there is nothing for a local check to be about. The sentence is the claim; somebody can disagree with it.

`<name>_unmirrored` — an author CAN trip it and nothing local checks it. Recorded debt, not an exemption: validate.mjs prints every one of these by name on every run. This is the state all three locale caps were in, silently, and the point of the sibling is that the next one is a visible blank instead.

ADDING A CAP: pick the sibling before the number is read anywhere. If it is `_mirrored_by`, the row in AstraPlugins has to land first and $ASTRA_PLUGINS_REF in .github/workflows/ingest.yml has to move to a commit carrying it — that pin is what build-index.yml checks the other repository out at, so a row added there reaches this comparison when the pin moves, not when it merges.

WHEN THE MIRROR CHECK GOES RED, DO NOT DELETE THE SIBLING. It greens in one keystroke by unpinning the number, and the cap goes on being enforced here either way — on an author who has already pushed a tag. That is the repair that destroys what the check was protecting — and it is now RED rather than green, because a cap with no sibling at all fails. Fix the copy, or move the pin.

WHAT THIS CANNOT REFUSE, stated so nobody believes otherwise: relabelling a true `_mirrored_by` as `_not_author_facing` with a false sentence greens everything, and no program can tell. That is the floor of any exemption list and it is the reason the sibling carries prose rather than a boolean — the escape hatch was made into a written claim somebody can read in a diff and disagree with, not closed. Measured: deleting a sibling is one keystroke and is red; writing a false one is a sentence and is green.

SCOPE: this covers the numeric caps in THIS file. Caps that live as `maxLength` in schema/version-v1.json are outside it — max_permission_reason_chars is mirrored from one, and that mirror line names a JSON pointer rather than a key. Nothing enumerates the schema's own caps in the mirrored-by direction, which is a smaller instance of exactly the gap the four siblings above close. AND IT RUNS THE OTHER WAY TOO, found 2026-08-23 while mirroring max_artifact_bytes: that cap's number is repeated as an artifact `size` `maximum` in BOTH schema/index-v1.json and schema/version-v1.json, and no reader compares either with this file. So this file can have copies in the schemas that nothing checks, as well as the schemas having caps here that nothing checks.
max_artifact_bytes_note:
256 MiB, the largest .astraplugin the registry will list. Deliberately below max_extract_bytes: a bundle whose COMPRESSED size approaches the daemon's UNCOMPRESSED extraction cap cannot install.

WAS `_unmirrored` UNTIL 2026-08-23, and the sentence it carried is kept here rather than deleted, because a retraction that erases its own claim leaves the next reader unable to tell a correction from a silent edit: `An author CAN trip this: astra-plugin build writes the .astraplugin and knows its size. Nothing in AstraPlugins names this number — grep for it there returns nothing — so a 300 MiB bundle builds, tags, uploads, and is refused here at the download step. It is recorded rather than fixed because fixing it is a cap on build, not a locale rule, and the review that found the locale three did not look at this one.` All of that was true. `astra-plugin build` now refuses over this cap and warns at half of it, and grep for 268435456 over there returns the row this sibling names.

THE FIRST READING OF THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WRONG, so read it twice: `deliberately below max_extract_bytes` does NOT mean the daemon's cap already covers this one. They are different units. 500 MiB UNCOMPRESSED and 256 MiB COMPRESSED leave a window an author reaches whenever the payload is already compressed — a model, audio, video, a packed data file — and `astra-plugin`'s pack-time refusal of max_extract_bytes says nothing about it. Constructed upstream on 2026-08-23: 314,572,800 incompressible bytes packed to 314,628,268, cleared max_extract_bytes by 200 MiB, and sat 44.1 MiB over this number.

TWO OTHER COPIES OF THIS NUMBER LIVE IN THIS REPOSITORY and nothing compares them with this key: the artifact `size` `maximum` in schema/index-v1.json and the one in schema/version-v1.json. Checked, not assumed, and stated precisely because the loose version of it is wrong: the ONLY code that reads either `maximum` is tools/lib/jsonschema.mjs, the generic validator, which enforces them against a document. Nothing anywhere COMPARES either with this key. The four-sibling convention covers the numeric caps in THIS file, so a schema copy that drifted from this key would be invisible to it. Raising max_artifact_bytes is three edits.
max_versions_per_plugin_not_author_facin: Counts the version records under one plugin in THIS catalogue. A source tree has one version at a time and no history of its own listings, so there is nothing local to count.
max_artifacts_per_version_not_author_fac: Counts the artifacts attached to one GitHub release. `astra-plugin build` packs one bundle per invocation and never sees the set; the matrix that produces them lives in a workflow, and the count is a property of the release rather than of any tree.
max_keywords_not_author_facing: Keywords are curator-set. bot/lib/derive.mjs:262 says it in as many words — categories, keywords and homepage are the fields no bundle carries — and this number is currently read by nothing in this repository either, which is its own small debt and a different one.
max_keyword_length_not_author_facing: Same field, same reason: no bundle carries a keyword for a cap to apply to.
typosquat_flag_distance_not_author_facin: An edit distance between one listing's id and the ids already in this catalogue. It is not a cap on anything an author writes; its other operand is the catalogue, which no source tree can see.
max_index_bytes_not_author_facing: The size of the whole generated registry/v1/index.json, which is this repository's own artifact. No single plugin owns it and no author can measure it.
max_index_bytes_note:
1 MiB, measured on `node tools/build-index.mjs --stdout`, which is byte-for-byte what the committed registry/v1/index.json holds before signing — both come from stableStringify, so there is no pretty-printing difference between them. That is the early measure. The signer holds the same number to the SIGNED catalogue, `issued_at`, `expires_at` and signatures included, because those are the bytes the service (SERVE-50) and every client refuse over 1 MiB: tools/signer/run.mjs measures them after signing (SERVE-49; ops couplings 155). The envelope added 239 bytes to the serial-54 catalogue with one signer, and every further signer adds its own. .github/workflows/build-index.yml compares the deploy candidate against this number; before it did, that step echoed `wc -c` and compared it to nothing, and notes/icon-readme-contract.md's `do not let the index quietly grow past a few megabytes` was enforced by nobody reading a log line.

TODAY, measured 2026-08-22 on 10 listings: 237,384 bytes. Icons are 54.6% of it, READMEs 23.6%, and all the card text together 0.36%. READ THIS BEFORE RAISING THE NUMBER: at ~23.7 KB per listing this ceiling arrives at roughly 44 listings, on ICON growth, long before locale growth reaches it. Nine locales of card text on every listing is single-digit percent; nine locales at the schema's own caps is at most 8 KiB per listing, which is what max_listing_i18n_bytes bounds, and 100 listings all at that cap is 800 KiB and would bust this too. Both cases point at the same fix, which notes/icon-readme-contract.md already sanctions: move icon_url and readme to *_url + *_sha256 pairs. Raising this number requires a written reason here.
max_icon_bytes_note:
8 KiB, the largest icon a NEW release may carry into the catalogue, as the decoded file (icon.png, .webp, .svg, .jpg, .jpeg or .ico) before base64. Enforced in bot/lib/derive.mjs through bot/lib/assets.mjs's checkIcon: an icon over it is DROPPED with W_ICON_DROPPED and the release publishes without it, the same as a hostile SVG, because a decorative file is not a gate on shipping software and from contract 3.0.0 no moderator is in the loop to wave one through. tools/validate.mjs holds every committed icon to it, except the ones named in max_icon_bytes_grandfathered.

WHY THIS NUMBER, measured on the signed catalogue at serial 55 (649,005 bytes, 16 listings, in the file's own pretty-printed form): inlined icons were 470,508 bytes of it, READMEs 96,348, everything else 81,092. So a listing without its icon averages 11,090 bytes (README 6,022, the rest 5,068). An icon at this cap is 10,946 bytes in the catalogue (4 x ceil(8192 / 3) of base64 plus the 22-byte data: prefix), so a listing whose icon is at the cap is 22,036 bytes and 47 of them fit under max_index_bytes beside the 1,058-byte envelope. Sixty AVERAGE listings fit with room: the ten raster icons in the catalogue re-encoded at 128x128 WebP quality 80 (the card is drawn at about 64 CSS pixels, so 128 device pixels on a 2x screen) weigh 1,142 to 6,346 bytes, mean 3,236, and with the six SVGs as they are the mean icon is 2,444 bytes, 3,282 inlined; 60 x (11,090 + 3,282) + 1,058 is 863,378 bytes, 82.3% of the cap and past tools/lib/index-budget.mjs's 75% warning, which is the point of the warning. The break-even for sixty is an average icon of 4,759 bytes.

WHY NOT SMALLER. 4 KiB would make sixty listings fit even with every icon at the cap (63), and it refuses real card art: sleep-pause-timer's icon is 6,346 bytes at 128x128 WebP q80 and still 4,424 at 96x96, below the card's own resolution. 6 KiB misses that same icon at 128x128 q80 by 202 bytes. 8 KiB is the smallest round number that admits every raster icon in the catalogue at the card's resolution with the guidance an author is given, with 1,846 bytes to spare, and the guidance has to work for everyone because nobody reads the listing before it is signed.

EXISTING LISTINGS: an icon committed before this cap keeps being inlined, byte for byte, until that listing's next release, which derives its icon fresh from the bundle like every other release and so meets this cap. Over it, that release publishes without an icon and the author is told why and what to do. The six listed ones cost 436,292 bytes of the serial-55 catalogue between them; re-exported to the cap or below they cost at most 65,676.

RAISING OR LOWERING IT is a shared-number change (ops dev/change-recipes.md R5): AstraPlugins/spec/listing-limits.yaml and the CLI's vendored copy carry it, `astra-plugin build` warns over it, and C20 compares the two repositories from both ends: tools/check-locales.py --rules C20 there, and checkMirroredListingLimits here through max_icon_bytes_mirrored_by. It stops mattering when icons leave the catalogue as URL + SHA-256 pairs (ops notes/coordinator/index-budget.md), which is the fix this cap only buys time for.

WAS `_unmirrored` UNTIL 2026-10-03, and the sentence it carried is kept here for the reason max_artifact_bytes_note gives: `An author CAN trip this from their own tree, and at this repository's AstraPlugins pin nothing local checks it. The copy exists upstream from AstraPlugins fdb4f342 (branch ap6/icon-cap): a `max_icon_bytes` row in spec/listing-limits.yaml and its vendored CLI copy, with `astra-plugin build` warning over it. This sibling becomes `_mirrored_by` in the commit that moves bot/manifest-probe/astra-plugins.pin to an AstraPlugins master commit carrying that row, and not before, because checkMirroredListingLimits reads the PINNED tree. The pin is not moved here on purpose: every master commit carrying the row also carries 05b4c28 (2026-09-30), which adds a `wakeword` capability to the manifest crate's CAPABILITY_NAMES that schema/version-v1.json's capability enum and bot/lib/policy/constants.mjs's KNOWN_AUTHORITY do not know (ops dev/change-recipes.md R4, half landed). Moving the pin would change how a manifest declaring it is judged, and that is its own reviewed change.` All of that was true. The pin moved to AstraPlugins d15c896 (#79's merge) once the `wakeword` capability it was waiting on had landed here, and checkMirroredListingLimits now refuses an `_unmirrored` cap whose row the pinned file carries, which is what made this flip a red build rather than a reminder. ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE OTHER `_mirrored_by` CAPS, said so that the $comment's definition is not read as a claim it is not: the copy makes `astra-plugin build` WARN over this cap, not refuse, because this registry's own answer is a dropped icon and a published release, not a refusal. What `_mirrored_by` holds here is the copy and its comparison in both directions.

max_icon_bytes_grandfathered.$comment: Icons committed before max_icon_bytes existed that are over it, by listing id and the SHA-256 of the exact committed file. tools/validate.mjs allows each of these, and nothing else over the cap, up to the old 131,072-byte ceiling (bot/lib/assets.mjs MAX_ICON_BYTES). An entry is NOT an exemption for the listing: its next release derives the icon from the bundle and meets max_icon_bytes like any other, and once the committed file stops matching, validate.mjs names the entry as stale so it can be deleted. Never add to this list; it only shrinks. Measured 2026-09-27 at registry 19e192a.

max_listing_i18n_bytes_note:
The whole `i18n` member of ONE listing, as UTF-8 JSON. A per-listing budget on purpose: a shared ceiling would let one verbose author stop every other author's publish behind a red catalogue build whose error names no plugin. Enforced in bot/lib/locales.mjs BEFORE the block is emitted.

IT IS A BACKSTOP, NOT A SHAPE, and the measurement says so. The worst case a correct listing reaches, with every code Astra can be set to (ten cards since `kk`, 2026-09-27): every card's name at 64 characters of three-byte text, because a brand keeps its own script in every language, and every summary at 200 characters of the widest letter in that language's own alphabet, because a summary is prose — 6,821 bytes, 1,371 under this number. What it catches is text outside the basic multilingual plane, a listing whose cards are nearly all in an alphabet wider than their languages use, or a per-string cap that stopped being enforced. DO NOT LOWER IT toward that 6,821: a ceiling below the legitimate worst case takes a correct CJK listing's translations away and explains it with a budget. bot/tests/ingest.test.mjs asserts the headroom in that direction, building the case from LOCALE_CODES and bot/lib/names.mjs's alphabets rather than from a list typed by hand.

THE STAND-IN THIS NOTE USED TO QUOTE STOPPED BEING AN UPPER BOUND AT THE TENTH CODE. It was every card in three-byte CJK, 7,399 bytes for nine, and the test built nine by hand. Ten such cards are 8,221 bytes, 29 over this number, and a Kazakh card is Cyrillic, so the stand-in was replaced by the script-aware case above rather than the number raised. If the all-CJK stand-in is wanted back as the guarantee, the fix is raising this number, and that is a shared-number change (ops dev/change-recipes.md R5): this key is `_mirrored_by` AstraPlugins/spec/listing-limits.yaml and the CLI's vendored copy, and C20 compares them from both ends.
max_locale_bytes_note: One locales/<code>.json in a bundle, checked on the raw bytes BEFORE JSON.parse. inspectBundle materialises every file the manifest lists as a Buffer bounded only by max_extract_bytes (500 MB); icons are capped at 8 KiB (max_icon_bytes; 128 KiB for the eight grandfathered below it) and READMEs at 16 KiB, and locale files were capped by nothing at all. A 200 MB flat-but-valid en.json would take the ingest runner out mid-derivation and leave the submitter's issue with no verdict — the one failure mode this bot must not have. 256 KiB is about fifty times the largest locale file in any example plugin.
max_locale_keys_note: Keys in one locale file, checked after the parse and before anything walks them. The parity rules compare key sets pairwise across every locale a bundle ships, so the work is quadratic in this number and the findings it can produce are linear in it; both are bounded here rather than discovered on a runner.
max_tree_object_bytes_not_author_facing: The size of one git tree object in THIS repository. The bot names what it writes under plugins/<id>/ itself, a fixed few files and one record per version, so nothing in an author's source tree decides how wide a tree here grows.
max_tree_object_bytes_note:
1 MiB: every tree object at a commit, the root tree included, as git stores it (`git cat-file -s`). tools/lib/tree-modes.mjs refuses one past it wherever the tree rule runs: tools/validate.mjs (CI and the Signer's catalogue gate), bot/publish-apply.mjs's own commit, and the five workflow writers' `node tools/lib/tree-modes.mjs HEAD` before their push (ops dev/couplings.md entry 215).

WHY IT EXISTS: the plugins service reads every commit on `main`, and its serial reader refuses a tree object over 8 MiB, after which `rev_list_count` cannot be asked at that commit or any later one. `main` is never rewritten, so one such commit would freeze the service's reading of every commit after it. The service relies on this number, so the contract names it too (B.4, from the version after 3.4.0).

WHY THIS NUMBER: a tree entry is its name plus 28 bytes, so 1 MiB is tens of thousands of names in one directory, an eighth of the service's bound and far past anything here. Measured 2026-10-03 at 8837648: the widest tree object is bot/lib at 1,785 bytes, the widest under a B.4 record root is plugins at 869, and no tree object in main's history is wider than 1,785.

RAISING IT is a contract change first, and tools/selftest/validation.mjs holds this key to the contract's number, so the edit here is red until both move.
max_listing_tree_entries_not_author_faci: Counts the entries beneath one plugins/<id>/ in THIS catalogue. They grow with its version records (max_versions_per_plugin), which no source tree has, and a fixed few files the bot writes beside them.
max_listing_tree_entries_note:
Entries beneath one plugins/<id>/, files and directories both, at every depth, as `git ls-tree -r -t` lists them. Refused past it where max_tree_object_bytes is, by the same rule (ops dev/couplings.md entry 215).

WHY IT EXISTS: the plugins service's mirror counts a listing's whole subtree against a 400,000-entry cap and refuses the listing past it. The service relies on this number, so the contract names it too (B.4, from the version after 3.4.0).

WHY THIS NUMBER: a listing holds plugin.json, identity.json, a README, at most six icons (bot/lib/assets.mjs ICON_FORMATS), versions/ and one record per version, so at max_versions_per_plugin (200) it is at most 210 entries, and 2,000 is nearly ten times that: max_versions_per_plugin is the cap a real listing meets first, and this one catches what that one cannot see, files a writer swept in beside the records. Measured 2026-10-03 at 8837648: the largest listing, companion-cat, holds 9 entries, and no listing in main's history held more.

RAISING IT is a contract change first, and tools/selftest/validation.mjs holds this key to the contract's number. That test also refuses max_versions_per_plugin past 1,990, where a listing's fullest tree would pass this bound and the tree rule would refuse a listing the version rule allows.
